source.title: Medicine Advertisements Board (MAB) 'Guideline on Advertising of Medicines and Medicinal Products to General Public' (MAB 3/2015, effective 1 Sep 2015); Medicines (Advertisement & Sale) Act 1956 (Act 290)
source.citation: MAB Guideline Parts 4-10 and Appendices 2-3; Act 290 ss.3, 4B, 5 and Schedule
source.last_reviewed_by: PENDING EXPERT REVIEW - transcribed from the primary MOH/MAB documents by an AI assistant on 2026-09-20; not yet reviewed by a qualified Malaysian regulatory professional. Note: this guideline is dated 2015 - confirm no later MAB revisions apply.

references.label: MAB Guideline on Advertising of Medicines and Medicinal Products to General Public (MAB 3/2015)
Medicines (Advertisement & Sale) Act 1956 (Act 290) - MOH Pharmaceutical Services
MOH Pharmaceutical Services - Medicine Advertisements Board (MAB)

permitted_claims.claim: Functional / indication claims that match EXACTLY the indication approved by the Drug Control Authority (DCA) for that registered product
permitted_claims.notes: MAB Guideline §6.1 - functional claims are allowed only for the ingredient claims approved by DCA. Advertising to the public is only allowed for DCA-registered products (§4.3).

permitted_claims.claim: Testimonials from real, identifiable users about approved indications
permitted_claims.notes: MAB Guideline §5.3 - allowed only with the statement 'The effect of the product may vary among individuals' and, for public testimonials, a consent letter (name, IC/passport no., signature, contact no.).
MAB Guideline §5.1 - allowed if the celebrity is responsible and accountable and the ad carries the statement 'The effect of the product may vary among individuals'.

permitted_claims.claim: Price-list style ads showing only the product picture (under 4cm x 5cm) and price, with the DCA registration number
permitted_claims.notes: MAB Guideline §10.7 - no MAB approval needed for such price lists.

permitted_claims.claim: Ads containing ONLY the product brand name, company name and/or logo
permitted_claims.notes: MAB Guideline §10.10 - exempt from MAB approval.

permitted_claims.claim: Contests, competitions and sponsorship linked to the brand without mentioning specific claims
Free gifts that are not the same as the advertised product (pen, mug, calculator, etc.)
permitted_claims.notes: MAB Guideline §10.6 - allowed, but the VALUE of the free gift may not be stated.

permitted_claims.claim: 'New' for a product or presentation registered in Malaysia for 18 months or less, or a specified new aspect (new look, new pack size) within 18 months of the DCA-approved change

prohibited_claims.claim: Any claim, direct or indirect, to prevent, treat, alleviate, cure or diagnose: kidney disease or defects, heart disease or defects, diabetes, epilepsy or fits, paralysis, tuberculosis, asthma, leprosy, cancer, deafness, drug addiction, hernia or rupture, eye diseases, hypertension, mental disorder, infertility, frigidity, impaired sexual function or impotency, venereal disease, or nervous debility from sexual intercourse
prohibited_claims.reason: These 20 conditions are scheduled in Act 290; advertising an article as a medicine or remedy for them is a criminal offence, and MAB does not allow them in public ads unless it approves.
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: Medicines (Advertisement & Sale) Act 1956 s.3(1) & Schedule; MAB Guideline §4.4(a) & Appendix 2

prohibited_claims.claim: Claims about contraception; improving the condition or functioning of the kidney or heart; improving sexual function or sexual performance; procuring miscarriage
prohibited_claims.reason: Prohibited by Act 290 s.3(1)(b)-(c) and MAB §4.4(b)-(d).
prohibited_claims.regulation_reference: Medicines (Advertisement & Sale) Act 1956 s.3(1)(b)-(c); MAB Guideline §4.4(b)-(d)

prohibited_claims.claim: Words or images that claim or imply the CURE of any ailment, illness or disease (other than relief of symptoms) - e.g. 'cures', 'complete cure', 'instant cure'
prohibited_claims.reason: Therapeutic claims of cure are not allowed unless approved by MAB.

prohibited_claims.claim: Banned superlative / hyperbole terms: anti-aging, anti-stress, aphrodisiac, arousal, complete cure, 'effective' (for traditional products and supplements), excellent, fabulous, fantastic, guaranteed, hormone releaser, ideal, instant cure, libido, longevity, miracle / miraculously / magic / magical, mythical, no side effect, perpetual youth, potent, powerful, saintly / heavenly, sensational relief, sexual powers, superior, 'the best' / 'the only' / 'the most', unique, wonders, world's best - and any synonyms
prohibited_claims.reason: MAB Appendix 3 lists these descriptors as not permissible; superlatives and hyperbole cannot be used to imply superiority (list is non-exhaustive).

prohibited_claims.claim: 'No. 1', any percentage figure (e.g. '98% satisfied') without substantiation
prohibited_claims.reason: Appendix 3 disallows 'No. 1' and 'any percentage' unless substantiated; statistical claims should be supported by Malaysian data where available.

prohibited_claims.claim: 'No side effects', 'no harmful effects', 'no toxic or adverse effects', 'placebo-like' safety; or suggesting safety/efficacy is due to being 'natural'
prohibited_claims.reason: Safety claims may not imply freedom from side effects; no medicine or medicinal product is completely risk free.

prohibited_claims.claim: Claims that a supplement will prevent, control, retard or reverse ageing; improve brain, memory, IQ or concentration; give immunity against specific diseases; prevent or reduce stress; improve sports or study performance
prohibited_claims.reason: Each is not acceptable unless the DCA has approved it in the product's registered indication.

prohibited_claims.claim: Quick weight loss results; fat-burning / thermogenic claims; 'eat as much as you like'
prohibited_claims.reason: Weight-management ads must balance effectiveness with healthy diet and exercise; quick weight loss and thermogenic (fat-burning) activity claims are not allowed.

prohibited_claims.claim: Doctors, dentists, pharmacists, scientists or nurses (or a white coat, stethoscope, clinical setting, 'recommended by doctors') giving an impression of professional or scientific advice or endorsement; references to a 'college', 'hospital' or 'laboratory'
prohibited_claims.reason: Impressions of professional endorsement are not allowed without written consent of the professional body.

prohibited_claims.claim: Claims naming tests or trials at a named hospital, clinic, institute, lab or college without that organisation's authorisation; pseudo-scientific jargon or misleading statistics, graphs or tables
prohibited_claims.reason: Research references are only permissible if authorised and must not be misused or given greater validity than they have.

prohibited_claims.claim: Improper, exaggerated or misleading before-and-after claims or visuals; visuals depicting a more serious condition than the indication
prohibited_claims.reason: Before/after claims must relate to the approved indication and severity; a declaration of originality must be held ready.

prohibited_claims.claim: Playing on fear, superstition or religion (e.g. 'you may get sick without this'); implying a condition will worsen without the product; inducing unwarranted anxiety
prohibited_claims.reason: Ads may not abuse trust, play on fear, exploit superstition or religious beliefs of any community.

prohibited_claims.claim: Misusing 'Halal', the Halal logo, Islamic imagery or Quranic verses to mislead
prohibited_claims.reason: Only JAKIM-recognised Halal certification may be shown; misuse of religious wording or verses is not allowed.

prohibited_claims.claim: Implying good health is jeopardised without vitamin supplementation, or that vitamins substitute for a balanced diet; encouraging unnecessary, excessive or indiscriminate use
prohibited_claims.reason: Ads must not encourage unnecessary purchase or use.

prohibited_claims.claim: Disparaging or attacking competitors, other products or the medical profession; comparative claims that identify a competitor or use baseless comparatives ('stronger', 'quicker')
prohibited_claims.reason: Comparative claims must be factual, fair and substantiated and must not disparage others.

prohibited_claims.claim: Suggesting a supplement or medicine is a food or cosmetic, or emphasising flavour/cosmetic attributes (delicious, tasty, beautify, whitening) so consumers think it is non-medicinal
prohibited_claims.reason: Ads should not lead consumers to believe a medicinal product is a food or cosmetic.

prohibited_claims.claim: Speed-of-action claims not supported by evidence or the approved label: 'instant' (about 10 seconds), 'fast' (about 30 minutes), 'all-day relief' (10+ hours), '24 hour relief', 'long-acting'
prohibited_claims.reason: Pharmacokinetic/speed claims are only acceptable if substantiated or on the approved label; the guideline defines what each term means.

prohibited_claims.claim: Calling a product 'herbal' unless the DCA-approved label says so; calling it 'natural' unless all components are naturally occurring
prohibited_claims.reason: Herbal and natural claims must comply with the DCA-approved label and the natural-claims rule.

prohibited_claims.claim: 'New' for a product registered in Malaysia for more than 18 months
prohibited_claims.reason: The word 'new' may not be used beyond 18 months from registration/approved change.

prohibited_claims.claim: Over-emphasising the manufacturer or foreign country of origin to promote efficacy
prohibited_claims.reason: Origin claims must not be used to promote efficacy.

prohibited_claims.claim: Stating the value of a free gift
prohibited_claims.reason: The value of a free gift may not be mentioned in the advertisement.

prohibited_claims.claim: Recommending supplements for pregnant or lactating women (other than some vitamins/minerals), or implying it is routine for pregnant women to take them
prohibited_claims.reason: Restricted; if pregnancy use is approved, ads must advise consulting a healthcare professional.

restricted_or_conditional_claims.claim: Advertising a DCA-registered supplement to the public at all
restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: The product must be DCA-registered, and the ad must be approved by the Medicine Advertisements Board (MAB); the approval certificate is valid for three calendar years and the ad must match the approved content exactly.
restricted_or_conditional_claims.regulation_reference: MAB Guideline §3.1, §3.3, §4.3; Act 290 s.4B; MOH Pharmaceutical Services MAB page

restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: Each ad must show the DCA registration number clearly plus the statement 'This is a medicine / supplement / traditional product advertisement' (choose as appropriate). Online ads must display the MAB approval (KKLIU) number on every approved page, with the advertiser's name, address and contact number.
Must include the statement 'This should be taken with a balanced diet and regular exercise.'

Must carry 'The effect of the product may vary among individuals'; the person must genuinely exist and be accountable; public testimonials need a signed consent letter; testimonials may only refer to approved indications.
Must be substantiated (evidence available on demand), preferably with Malaysian data, and must not be presented as more valid than they are.
Only allowed if that ingredient reference has been approved by the DCA for the package insert.

restricted_or_conditional_claims.claim: Health-education / advertorial content on an ingredient (e.g. ginseng, tongkat ali, vitamin C)
restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: Allowed without MAB approval only if it does not mention the product, brand, pictures or website and includes advice to seek professional healthcare advice; it must not be placed next to an ad for a product with that ingredient.

restricted_or_conditional_claims.claim: Ads that mix approved supplement claims with non-approved products (food, cosmetics, devices)
restricted_or_conditional_claims.condition: MAB-approved ads must not share the same space as ads that do not need MAB approval; where shown together the border must clearly separate them.

Contravening Act 290 ss.3, 4, 4A or 4B: first conviction fine up to RM3,000 and/or up to 1 year's imprisonment; subsequent conviction fine up to RM5,000 and/or up to 2 years (text as published by MOH; confirm the current amounts).
